final.text: Extended reality refers to extending reality by some means intuitively or using systems to augment reality or replace the perception of reality systemically.

The reality-virtuality continuum consists of one end where reality is completely replaced with virtual reality systems, the other end where virtuality is completely replaced by the entirely real world, and mixed reality or augmented reality concepts in between.
The reality-virtuality continuum was taken from the 1994 paper "A Taxonomy of Mixed Reality Visual Displays" by Paul Milgram and Fumio Kishino.
The broad objective of the course is to learn about virtual reality, augmented reality, and allied concepts to master the development and deployment of systems.
The course covers a basic understanding of all relevant concepts, a theoretical background to build a foundation in the field, and practical knowledge on development and deployment.
The course uses case studies involving game engines and software development kits to explain how to develop and deploy technologies.
The course covers how senses influence the use of technology and systems through an understanding of cognitive and psychological aspects.

The theoretical background of the technology includes building interactive software, building interactive virtual reality or augmented reality systems, software functionality, software components, hardware operation, hardware technologies, and designing and implementing interactions.
The course uses a case study of a virtual reality system related to a digital heritage preservation project.
